notes.meaning: Abraham's servant asks the young woman who her father is and whether his party can lodge at her family home. He had already rewarded her kindness with jewelry, but now he needed to know if she was from Abraham's family.
Rebekah shares her family line, explaining that her grandfather Nahor was Abraham's brother. This means she is closely related to Abraham, making her a cousin to Isaac.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars observe that the family tree places Rebekah in the generation after Isaac rather than in his own generation.

notes.meaning: Rebekah warmly offers lodging and supplies for both the men and their animals. Her ready hospitality shows that she comes from a generous family with plenty of room and feed to spare.
Hearing her answer, the servant bows his head and prostrates himself to the ground in worship. He stops right there to thank God, recognizing that the Lord has answered his prayers.

The servant praises the Lord for showing faithful love and keeping His promises to Abraham. He rejoices that God led him straight to the home of his master's own relatives instead of leaving the journey to chance.

Rebekah runs ahead to tell her mother and the other women in the house what happened. In large households of that era, the women lived in their own quarters, making her mother the first person to hear the news.

Rebekah's brother Laban rushes out to the spring to meet the traveler. He hurries after seeing the expensive gold jewelry on his sister's wrists and hearing her story, showing an eager interest in the wealthy guest.
Laban welcomes the servant warmly, calling him blessed by the Lord. He invites him inside and assures him that space has already been prepared for both the men and their camels.
Laban brings the servant inside, unloads the camels, and provides straw and feed for the animals. He also offers water so the servant and the men traveling with him can wash their tired feet.
Even though food is set before him, the servant refuses to eat until he explains his mission. He puts his master's business ahead of his own hunger and rest.
The servant introduces himself simply by stating that he serves Abraham. This announcement immediately connects him to the family's famous relative and sets the stage for his message.
The servant explains how the Lord has greatly blessed Abraham with wealth, livestock, precious metals, and servants. He credits all this prosperity to God rather than to human luck or skill.

The servant tells the family that Sarah gave birth to Isaac in her old age and that Abraham has given him the entire estate. This news shows that Isaac is the sole heir and fully able to provide for a wife.
The servant explains the solemn promise Abraham required of him. He was forbidden from choosing a local Canaanite wife for Isaac and was told instead to travel all the way to Abraham's own relatives.
The servant recounts the practical question he raised before leaving home. He had wondered what would happen if the young woman was unwilling to leave her family and follow him to Canaan.

Abraham had answered with strong faith, assuring the servant that the Lord would send His angel to make the mission a success. Abraham walked closely with God in daily obedience, trusting that God would provide a wife from his own relatives.

Abraham promised that if the relatives refused to send a daughter, the servant would be completely free from his oath. This shows the servant acted honestly and without trying to force anyone into the marriage.
The servant recounts his prayer at the well, where he asked God to grant success to his journey. He approached God with humble trust, asking the Lord of his master to guide the outcome.

The servant explains the specific sign he asked from God at the well. He asked that the woman chosen for Isaac would not only offer him a drink, but would also volunteer to draw water for all ten camels, showing kindness and hard work.
Before the servant even finished his silent prayer, Rebekah arrived at the well with her water jar. Her quick arrival proved to him that God had already heard his heart and was answering his request.
